title: Lumbopelvic ratio L/P vs % trunk motion, right and left axial rotation, obese young males
condition: obese healthy males, standing, right and left axial rotation

quantity.name: lumbopelvic ratio L/P
quantity.definition: total lumbar rotation / total pelvis rotation at 10% steps of full trunk motion (cumulative from upright)

source.sample: 18 young healthy males: 9 normal-weight (BMI 23.9 SD 1.3) and 9 age/height-matched obese (BMI 35.3 SD 2.6); no recent back pain

protocol.summary: L/P at ten intervals of trunk motion during maximal voluntary right and left axial rotation (Fig 6ef), obese group.
how_to_use: Normalise the target trunk angle by the full trunk RoM in that direction (kinematics.ghasemi2021.rom_trunk_obese) and pick the 10% interval.
Split the pelvis+lumbar rotation as pelvis = trunk/(1+L/P), lumbar = trunk - pelvis (here trunk = thorax vs lab, lumbar = thorax vs pelvis, so trunk = pelvis + lumbar).
L/P is cumulative (total angles from upright), not incremental; interpolate linearly between interval end points.
Use the obese values only for obese subject models; the flexion/extension rhythm did not differ between groups.
Use SD for robustness runs; data are young males only.

measurement.device: 10-camera Vicon, Plug-in-Gait markers + thoracic (C7,T10,CLAV,STRN) and pelvic (ASIS/PSIS) clusters; XYZ Euler angles of thorax and pelvis vs lab, lumbar = thorax relative to pelvis
measurement.posture: standing, knees extended, no feet pivoting
measurement.task: maximal voluntary flexion, extension, right/left lateral bending, right/left axial rotation from relaxed upright standing, unloaded

protocol.notes: L/P = total lumbar rotation / total pelvis rotation (both cumulative from upright, in the plane of motion), at 10..100% of the full trunk motion (same in-house code as Tafazzol 2014 / Narimani 2018). Obese right rotation 80-100% error bars are inside the marker (SD < ~0.09) -> sd null; obese left 100% SD hidden; 10% left-rotation lower bars clipped at 0 (SD from upper cap). L/P < 1: pelvis rotates more than lumbar spine in axial rotation. Group effect significant (p~0.02, ~37% lower in obese) for right/left lateral bending and right axial rotation; not significant for flexion, extension, left rotation (Table 1 ANOVA). No group x interval interaction.

extraction.uncertainty: 6e: means ±0.02, SD ±0.04 (175 px per unit); 6f: means ±0.02 (normal 60% hidden behind obese marker ±0.04), SD ±0.04
extraction.check_notes: Digitised by colour segmentation at 300 dpi (red filled circles = opened red mask centroids; open blue squares = border-template match ignoring red-covered pixels; caps = extreme rows of coloured horizontal segments). SD = half cap-to-cap distance, or |cap - mean| when one cap was hidden. Independent manual re-check: 6a obese 10% circle rows 1215-1238 -> 3.24 (vs 3.25); 6c normal 50% square edges 1738/1760 -> 5.31 (vs 5.31).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
